comparison: Perfect agreement on stem-loop MicroC observations (C8-C10, C24-C29). Both evaluations find the volcano triangle topology, plume, reduced eve-neighbor contacts, and enhanced TL-TM contacts well-supported. Peer reviewers call evidence 'solid' and 'high-quality,' matching OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating.

Perfect agreement on lambda DNA replacement demonstrating loss of boundary function (C11-C13, C33-C43). Both evaluations accept the MicroC, virtual 4C, HCR-FISH, and cuticle analysis evidence. Peer reviewers request more methodological detail but do not challenge core findings, consistent with OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating.

Strong agreement on foundational claims about TAD formation and boundary pairing (C5-C7, C22-C23). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a 'major finding' and note it confirms models from prior genetic work. Both evaluations support these structural claims, though peer review emphasizes this as novel demonstration while OpenEval notes consistency with prior literature.

Strong agreement on nhomie reverse replacement converting stem-loop to circle-loop topology (C14-C16, C44-C50). Both evaluations find MicroC evidence of topology conversion well-supported. Peer reviewers call this 'An important finding,' matching OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating. Shared claims C56-C59 also covered.

Agreement on regulatory disruption in circle-loop configurations (C17, C51-C54). Both evaluations accept HCR-FISH and cuticle defect evidence. Peer reviewers note effects are 'modest' and request methodological detail, but accept findings as significant. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review also accepts with minor reservations about quantification.

Agreement on homie forward replacement showing circle-loop regulatory phenotypes (C60-C63). Both evaluations accept weak activation of flanking genes and developmental defects. Peer reviewers emphasize this demonstrates 'compromised regulatory boundary activity despite the presence of an eve TAD,' consistent with OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating.

Agreement on Abd-B MicroC observations showing circle-loop characteristics (C30-C32). Both evaluations accept the descriptive MicroC patterns showing LDC domains and progressive interactions. Neither challenges these observations, though OpenEval notes head-to-head pairing (C23) is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

Disagreement on TAD stability across developmental stages (C84-C87). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding strong evidence that TAD structure persists despite transcriptional changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting contact maps represent mixed cell populations and that single-cell studies show TADs may be absent, challenging the static structure interpretation.

Agreement on uncertainty about genome-wide prevalence (C71-C73). Both evaluations express caution about generalizing from ~30 volcano/plume TADs to genome-wide conclusions. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting ambiguous contact pattern interpretations; peer reviewers explicitly state 'generalizability...remains unclear' and call for untargeted approaches.

Agreement on meta-loop MicroC observations (C88-C90). Both evaluations accept the descriptive patterns showing rectangular interaction boxes diagnostic of head-to-head pairing. Neither challenges these specific observations, treating them as supporting evidence for boundary pairing mechanisms.

Agreement on complex meta-loop structures (C91-C95). Both evaluations accept the MicroC patterns showing four-boundary structures with head-to-tail pairing. Neither disputes these observations, which serve as additional genome-wide validation of the boundary pairing model.

Disagreement on mechanistic implications (C74-C75). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting logical inference that circle-loops exclude loop extrusion but requiring validation. Peer reviewers express stronger reservations (UNCERTAIN), emphasizing that 'boundary pairing is one of several mechanisms' and that 'functional interplay...remains to be further investigated.'

Disagreement on loop extrusion model critique (C76-C79). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting reinterpretation of published data requires direct validation. Peer reviewers express significant skepticism (UNCERTAIN), critiquing lack of consideration of alternative mechanisms and stating authors provide 'no consideration...to important biophysical properties.'

Disagreement on mammalian MicroC reanalysis (C80-C82). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting intriguing patterns but requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers express implicit skepticism (UNCERTAIN) through broader critique of mechanistic framework, citing compartmentalization models as alternative explanations for contact maps.

Agreement on foundational background claims (C19-C22, C64-C70). Both evaluations accept these as established knowledge from prior literature. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting well-established properties; peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting work 'confirms a model...posited based on extensive prior genetic work.'

Agreement on basic TAD formation principles (C1-C4). Both evaluations accept these foundational claims about Drosophila TAD formation from prior literature. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as well-established background; peer reviewers accept as established context without challenge.

OpenEval includes descriptive claim about A/B compartment model (C83) as background context for Discussion critique. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this is purely descriptive background rather than a study result.

Partial overlap on circle-loop characteristics (C56-C59). OpenEval R6 addresses homie forward replacement showing circle-loop properties; peer R4 addresses both nhomie reverse and homie forward replacements. Both evaluations support the convergent evidence from multiple circle-loop configurations.
